questions.q: Which payment method does NOT require a supplier bank account to be on file?
questions.explain: A check payment is printed and mailed without requiring a stored bank account on the supplier record.

questions.q: What additional detail does an international electronic payment require beyond a domestic one?
options: A specific bank and branch identified on the account
questions.explain: Cross-border electronic payments need a specific bank and branch identified, not just an account number.

questions.q: Why does Oracle Fusion mask a stored bank account number by default?
options: As a security control, so casual viewing shows only part of the number (e.g. the last four digits) while the full number remains stored for processing
Because the full number is never actually stored
Because masked numbers process payments faster
Because unmasked numbers are illegal to store
questions.explain: Masking is a security control over display; the full account number remains stored for actual payment processing.

questions.q: An invoice validates and gets approved normally, but the supplier is never paid. Where should you look first if the supplier uses electronic payment?
questions.explain: A missing or incomplete bank account surfaces as a payment-stage failure, not a validation-stage one — the invoice itself can look perfectly fine.

questions.q: Brightfield's fictional supplier Nordwell Freight Partners is overseas and missing bank and branch details. What is the most likely outcome if Brightfield tries to pay them electronically?
options: The payment succeeds using only the account number
Nordwell is automatically converted to a domestic supplier
The electronic payment is likely to fail because international payments require both a bank and branch
questions.explain: International electronic payments require both a bank and branch on the account; missing either is likely to cause a payment failure.
